aspects.says: A lambda copies the values of the locals it captures when it is created; for a reference that is the reference, so the object behind it can still change.
basis: section:A Lambda Copies the Locals It Uses, So They Must Be Effectively Final

aspects.says: A lambda may use a local only if it is effectively final: any second assignment, even after the lambda, is a compile error.
basis: section:A Lambda Copies the Locals It Uses, So They Must Be Effectively Final
aspects.reason: a rule the compiler enforces has no wrong solution that compiles; the export-tasks practice grades what capture by value means instead

aspects.says: A lambda that uses a field captures this and reads the field when it runs; a field copied into a local first is frozen at that moment.
basis: section:A Lambda Adds No Scope: `this` and Every Name Mean What They Mean Outside It

aspects.says: The lambda's class is a hidden class spun at run time by LambdaMetafactory, named Outer$$Lambda/0x..., which is not stable between runs.
basis: section:The Compiler Turns a Lambda Into a Private Method and an invokedynamic Call
aspects.reason: a property of the runtime's class naming that no test of the reader's code can observe; shown by the run on the page

aspects.says: An int[] or AtomicInteger holder gets around the effectively-final rule; the array loses updates under a parallel stream, AtomicInteger contends, and a stream reduction needs no shared state.
basis: section:A Lambda Copies the Locals It Uses, So They Must Be Effectively Final

aspects.says: Whether evaluating a lambda gives a new object is unspecified; on HotSpot a non-capturing lambda from one site is reused and a capturing one is new, so code must not rely on either.
basis: section:A Lambda's Identity Is Not Promised: Keep the Instance You Need to Find Again

aspects.says: Two lambda expressions with the same text are different objects, so a listener must be removed with the instance that was added.
basis: section:A Lambda's Identity Is Not Promised: Keep the Instance You Need to Find Again

aspects.says: A lambda's parameters and locals cannot reuse the name of a local of the enclosing method, which an anonymous class's method may.
basis: section:A Lambda Adds No Scope: `this` and Every Name Mean What They Mean Outside It
aspects.reason: a rule the compiler enforces has no wrong solution that compiles; the page shows the javac errors

aspects.says: Where no functional interface is expected (var, Object), a lambda does not compile.
basis: section:A Lambda Is an Object of Whatever Interface Its Context Expects
aspects.reason: a rule the compiler enforces has no wrong solution that compiles, so no test can grade it; the page shows both javac errors

aspects.says: javac compiles a lambda body into a private lambda$ method of the enclosing class and the lambda site into invokedynamic; it writes no class file, unlike an anonymous class.
basis: section:The Compiler Turns a Lambda Into a Private Method and an invokedynamic Call

aspects.says: A lambda is an instance of the functional interface its context expects; the same text gives objects of unrelated interfaces, and a cast between them fails at run time.
basis: section:A Lambda Is an Object of Whatever Interface Its Context Expects

aspects.says: Inside a lambda, this and unqualified methods mean the enclosing instance; inside an anonymous class they mean the anonymous object.
basis: section:A Lambda Adds No Scope: `this` and Every Name Mean What They Mean Outside It
